signals.topic: Bedrock SSE streaming raises unhandled ValueError on non-200 responses — blocks stream consumption
signals.summary: When Bedrock returns error responses in SSE events (e.g., 400 internalServerException), the SDK raises a raw ValueError instead of retrying or surfacing a proper APIStatusError, crashing the stream iterator.
aliases: bedrock stream crash on error response
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocked: streaming response iterator crashes with unhandled ValueError on Bedrock error responses. Stream consumption is a core workflow. Clear stack trace and proposed fix (retry or APIStatusError).

source_issues.title: Bedrock streaming SSE events errors are not handled gracefully
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace: ValueError raised at _stream_decoder.py line 58. User's stream iterator crashes. No retry, no APIStatusError. SDK v0.96.0, Python 3.12.

signals.topic: JSON mode requires fabricating nonsensical tool_use/tool_result blocks — breaks multi-turn streaming
signals.summary: Using JSON mode forces users to create fake tool_use blocks, and continuing the conversation requires fabricating a tool_result block. This prevents legitimate multi-turn streaming use cases and requires non-obvious workarounds.
signals.review_reason: API design flaw blocks a core use case: multi-turn conversation continuation with JSON-mode structured output. Users must fabricate tool blocks to satisfy API validation, which is non-obvious. Confirmed via API error responses. Affects any SDK consumer implementing structured output in streaming chat.

source_issues.title: Anthropic JSON Mode requires client to fabricate a nonsensical tool_use block
source_issues.evidence: API rejects conversation with JSON-mode tool_use without corresponding tool_result; rejects conversation with fabricated tool_result. Breaks multi-turn streaming. Workaround requires synthesizing fake tool blocks. Confirmed by API error responses.

signals.topic: SDK does not support Entra ID / short-lived bearer tokens — blocks enterprise procurement
signals.summary: The Python SDK captures auth_token once at construction. Enterprise customers using Microsoft Entra ID (1h token TTL) get 401 Unauthorized in long-running processes with no in-SDK refresh mechanism.
signals.review_reason: Blocks enterprise procurement: enterprise security/compliance reviews flag long-lived API keys as non-starters. Users are forced to subclass the SDK to get token refresh, which is a clear sign the feature is missing from the SDK surface. Workaround code is explicitly described as '12 lines every customer has to copy.'

source_issues.title: Support Entra ID and other short-lived bearer tokens for enterprise auth
source_issues.evidence: SDK reads auth_token once at __init__. Entra tokens expire ~1h. Users must subclass Anthropic (12-line workaround shown) to get token refresh. Blocked enterprise procurement documented.

signals.topic: toolRunner drops defaultHeaders on follow-up requests, breaking proxy/gateway authentication (including Cloudflare AI Gateway)
signals.summary: toolRunner helper fails to forward defaultHeaders on subsequent API calls during the tool-use loop. After the first turn, all custom headers (auth tokens, proxy keys) are dropped, causing authentication_error on every follow-up request. This makes toolRunner unusable behind Cloudflare AI Gateway or any header-based proxy, forcing users to implement the loop manually.
aliases: toolRunner defaultHeaders dropped on follow-up calls
toolRunner loses custom headers on subsequent requests
toolRunner breaks Cloudflare AI Gateway authentication
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed SDK bug with explicit user impact: toolRunner silently drops all defaultHeaders on every follow-up API call, causing authentication failures that block the entire multi-turn tool-use workflow. Users are forced to abandon the toolRunner helper entirely and reimplement it manually — there is no SDK-side workaround. Confirmed by Cloudflare team. Production-blocking for anyone using Cloudflare AI Gateway or any header-authenticated proxy with toolRunner.

source_issues.title: `toolRunner` drops `defaultHeaders` on follow-up requests (breaks proxy/gateway setups)
source_issues.evidence: User reports 400 authentication_error 'x-api-key header is required' on follow-up requests from toolRunner. Cloudflare team confirmed it as an SDK-side bug. Affects Cloudflare AI Gateway unified billing (cf-aig-authorization header). Single messages.create calls work fine; only toolRunner's internal loop is affected. No SDK-side workaround exists besides manually reimplementing the tool-use loop.

signals.topic: Model regression on Bedrock corrupts tool input_json strings with literal `<<<SENTINEL\n` prefix
signals.summary: claude-opus-4-7 deployed on AWS Bedrock emits a literal `<<<SENTINEL\n` prefix on every string value in tool input_json, persisting across multiple separate inference calls in the same thread. This corrupts tool outputs (e.g., file contents begin with the literal marker), affecting at least 12 distinct file paths across multiple tool_use blocks.
aliases: Bedrock model regression corrupts tool call string outputs
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed model-level regression that directly corrupts tool-use outputs. Every string value in the tool's input_json is prefixed with '<<<SENTINEL\n', rendering the output unusable (e.g., files would be written with the literal marker). The issue reproduces across multiple separate inference calls, not just a single streaming glitch. Confirmed as originating from the model/API layer before any SDK parsing.

source_issues.title: claude-opus-4-7 (Bedrock) emits literal `<<<SENTINEL\n` prefix on every string value inside a single tool's input_json (Bedrock)
source_issues.evidence: User reports literal '<<<SENTINEL\n' prepended to every string value in tool input_json across 5+ separate Bedrock inference calls. Approximately 12 distinct file paths corrupted in createOrOverrideFiles tool. Raw API response captured before any SDK parsing confirms corruption originates from the model/API layer. The marker is absent from system prompt, tool descriptions, message history, and the user's codebase.

signals.topic: MCP servers have no graceful degradation: one unreachable server atomically fails the entire request
signals.summary: When any configured MCP server is unreachable, the entire messages API request fails with HTTP 400 regardless of whether other servers are healthy. There is no optional flag, no per-server timeout, and the error message does not identify which server failed. This makes production deployments injecting multiple MCP servers extremely fragile — a transient outage on one tunnel or self-hosted service takes down the entire call path.
aliases: one unreachable MCP server fails entire request
signals.review_reason: While this is framed as a feature request, it is effectively a production-blocking gap: MCP server composition is an advertised capability, yet one transiently unreachable server causes the entire request to fail atomically. No workaround is viable client-side (pre-flight probes introduce SSRF/DNS rebinding risks; catch-and-retry is non-contractual). This blocks production deployments that use MCP servers with realistic uptime expectations (cloud tunnels, ephemeral services, third-party endpoints).

source_issues.title: API: mcp_servers[].optional flag + structured error for graceful degradation on unreachable injected MCP servers
source_issues.evidence: User reports 400 error 'Connection error while communicating with MCP server' when any one MCP server is unreachable. The request fails atomically — the healthy server is never reached. Affects production deployments with multiple MCP servers (filesystem + search + domain-specific). Confirmed on multiple model versions (haiku, sonnet, opus) and SDK versions (0.91, 0.92). Client-side workarounds (pre-flight probes, catch-and-retry) are fundamentally unreliable (SSRF, DNS rebinding, TOCTOU, race conditions).

signals.topic: Bundled Claude binary hangs when stdout is not a TTY (blocks CI/CD, Docker, orchestrators, headless environments)
signals.summary: The SDK subprocess hangs indefinitely when stdout is redirected (piped, file, or non-TTY environment) instead of a real terminal. This completely blocks use in CI runners, Docker containers without -t, launchd/cron jobs, and orchestrators that capture output via subprocess.PIPE. Combined with rate-limit event handling that also hangs, this causes silent indefinite hangs with zero diagnostic output. Users must wrap the process in `script -q /dev/null` as a workaround.
aliases: TTY-required subprocess behavior blocks headless environments
signals.review_reason: This is a high-impact production blocker. The bundled Claude binary's isatty() check makes the SDK unusable in any non-TTY environment — the exact environments where SDK consumers (CI pipelines, Docker, orchestrators) run. Combined with the RateLimitEvent hang (also noted in the same issue), users see silent indefinite hangs with no diagnostic output and no error, causing workflow timeouts. Strong user impact: a production launchd pipeline wasted 24+ hours of compute time before diagnosis.

source_issues.title: Bundled `claude` binary hangs when stdout is not a TTY (pipe / file / launchd / cron / Docker)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed 100% repro: `python tty_bug.py` completes in ~2s; `python tty_bug.py | cat` hangs indefinitely. Affects CI/GitHub Actions (piped stdout), Docker without -t, launchd/cron jobs, and orchestrators using subprocess.PIPE. Real production impact: a launchd-driven nightly pipeline timed out at 1800s every tick for 24+ hours.

signals.topic: SDK subprocess stderr output is silently lost when user-provided stderr callback raises (breaks debugging of CLI errors)
signals.summary: The stderr callback is wrapped in a bare `except Exception: pass` outside the stderr processing loop. When the user's callback raises even once, the entire `_handle_stderr` loop terminates and all subsequent stderr lines are silently dropped for the rest of the session. Subsequent CLI errors that would inform the user about failures are completely lost, making diagnosis impossible.
aliases: stderr callback exception kills stderr stream
_handle_stderr loop silently exits on callback error
signals.review_reason: A single stderr callback error permanently disables all stderr delivery for the rest of the session. The `except Exception: pass` is silent — no log, no traceback, no indication anything went wrong. This directly breaks the primary debugging channel for subprocess errors in a deterministic, reproducible way (any user callback that raises, even transiently, causes total stderr loss).

source_issues.title: Bug: stderr callback raise silently kills _handle_stderr loop, dropping all subsequent stderr lines
source_issues.evidence: 100% repro with 5/5 consecutive runs: mock stderr with 2 lines, callback raises RuntimeError on first line -> only 1 of 2 lines processed, second line dropped, function returns normally with no log or traceback. Subsequent CLI errors that would inform users about failures are permanently lost for the rest of the session.

signals.topic: Bundled Claude binary v2.1.121 is protocol-incompatible in container environments, causing silent 60-second timeout
signals.summary: Inside Docker containers, the bundled Claude binary (v2.1.121) does not respond to the SDK's `control_request:initialize` message, causing a silent 60-second timeout. The SDK's `_find_cli` prioritizes the bundled binary over PATH, so even if a working newer version exists on the host, the broken bundled version is used first. Users must manually bind-mount a newer binary over the bundled path as a workaround.
aliases: bundled CLI fails in container env
signals.review_reason: Makes the SDK completely unusable in any Docker/containerized environment with the affected bundled binary version. Silent 60-second timeout with no actionable error message means users cannot use the SDK inside the very container environments (CI runners, cloud builds) that are its primary deployment targets. This is a high-confidence, high-impact production blocker.

source_issues.title: _bundled/claude v2.1.121 protocol-incompatible in container env (silent timeout on control_request:initialize)
source_issues.evidence: Specific container image confirmed affected: `ghcr.io/vectorize-io/hindsight@sha256:...` (v0.5.6 standalone). Bundled binary reports v2.1.121 and fails silently for 60 seconds. Workaround: bind-mount host claude v2.1.128 over SDK bundled path. Any SDK consumer in a containerized environment hits a silent 60s timeout with no actionable error message.

signals.topic: MCP dependency vulnerability (CVE-2025-66416/GHSA-9h52-p55h-vw2f): SDK allows installing mcp 1.19.0-1.22.x without DNS rebinding protection
signals.summary: The SDK's declared dependency is `mcp>=1.19.0`, which allows versions 1.19.0-1.22.x. Those versions lack DNS rebinding protection for HTTP-based localhost MCP servers (CVE-2025-66416). Users whose applications use HTTP-based local MCP servers without authentication are exposed. The fix is trivial (`mcp>=1.23.0`), but new installations currently pull vulnerable versions.
aliases: outdated MCP dependency with security advisory
DNS rebinding protection missing in mcp<1.23.0
signals.review_reason: Despite being a dependency-level vulnerability, this has clear user impact: any SDK consumer using HTTP-based local MCP servers (a common pattern) without authentication is exposed to DNS rebinding attacks in the range of affected MCP versions. The vulnerability is public, the fix is known, and new SDK installations currently resolve to a vulnerable MCP version by default.

source_issues.title: Tighten mcp dependency to >=1.23.0 due to CVE-2025-66416
source_issues.evidence: SDK declares `mcp>=1.19.0` in pyproject.toml, allowing versions 1.19.0-1.22.x which are affected by public advisory CVE-2025-66416. MCP Python SDK did not enable DNS rebinding protection by default for HTTP-based localhost MCP servers before mcp==1.23.0. Affects applications using HTTP-based local MCP servers without authentication.

signals.topic: Long-running subprocess crashes leave stderr inaccessible — failures are completely undiagnosable
signals.summary: When the underlying Claude Code CLI subprocess exits non-zero (observed at exactly 61 turns with heavy MCP polling), the SDK surfaces only 'Command failed with exit code 1' and 'Check stderr output for details'. However, the subprocess stderr is not exposed to the consumer at all — there is no flag, hook, or attribute on the exception to retrieve it. Users cannot determine why the subprocess crashed and must implement elaborate workarounds to preserve state before the crash window.
signals.review_reason: While substantive work is preserved (commits/pushes survive), the inability to diagnose why the subprocess crashed means users cannot implement proper error handling or recovery. The error message tells users to check stderr but provides zero access to it. The 61-turn coincidence is also unexplained. This is an observability and recoverability gap that forces users into awkward workarounds.

source_issues.title: SDK subprocess crash during long-running queries with heavy MCP polling — stderr swallowed, error message uninformative
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced twice with identical stack trace at exactly 61 turns in two unrelated agent sessions. The error message itself says 'Check stderr output for details' but the SDK doesn't expose subprocess stderr to consumers. No flag, hook, or attribute to retrieve stderr. Workaround: push early/push often every 2-3 turns to preserve state before the crash window.

signals.topic: Uncaught EPIPE exception kills host process during subprocess restart race condition
signals.summary: When the SDK subprocess crashes during startup, a race between the subprocess exiting and parent stdin write causes an uncaught EPIPE that calls process.exit(1), killing the entire host application unless a defensive global handler is installed. Real production incident documented: 92s full-gateway downtime, all in-flight sessions lost, mid-cron jobs orphaned.
signals.review_reason: Count=1, but P0 justified by production downtime evidence: 92s full-gateway outage, session loss, orphaned jobs. The crash is a race condition in the SDK's own stdin write path — host applications without a specific defensive handler will crash. This is a primary workflow blocker for persistent-session mode users.

source_issues.title: Uncaught EPIPE from subprocess stdin write callback during startup-crash → fresh-retry race (v0.2.120)
source_issues.evidence: Production incident: 92s downtime, all in-flight sessions lost, orphaned mid-cron jobs. EPIPE arrives with no JS frame and no .catch(), exits process directly unless host installs defensive uncaughtException handler.

signals.topic: Slash command XML wrapper leaked into session transcript and returned verbatim on resume
signals.summary: Slash command inputs are wrapped in XML before being persisted to the JSONL transcript. On session resume via query({resume}) or getSessionMessages(), that internal XML wrapper is returned as the user-message text verbatim. Chat UIs render raw XML to users after page reload, and if consumers re-send this as input the model receives tag soup it cannot act on.
aliases: getSessionMessages returns XML instead of clean text
signals.review_reason: SDK consumers building chat UIs or IDE integrations with session resume are affected. The wrapper corrupts both UI display and model context. Workaround requires brittle regex against undocumented internal format. Clearly impacts session state integrity.

source_issues.title: Slash command XML wrapper persists in session transcript and leaks through resumed history
source_issues.evidence: Every SDK consumer that exposes slash commands and supports session resume hits this. Chat UIs render raw XML tags after page reload; consumers re-send corrupted input to the model. Users must write brittle regex-based workarounds against undocumented internal serialisation.

signals.topic: Options.agent silently falls back to default Claude when agent name refers to a plugin-loaded agent
signals.summary: The Options.agent parameter does not resolve plugin-loaded agent names, unlike the CLI's --agent flag. Instead of erroring or warning, it silently falls back to the default Claude model. Users get wrong agent responses with no indication of misconfiguration. Verified with repro showing CLI works correctly but SDK silently uses wrong agent.
aliases: plugin agent name not resolved in SDK options
agent option silently ignored for plugin agents
signals.review_reason: Silent failure mode is worse than crashing — users trust they are using a specific agent but receive default Claude with no signal that anything went wrong. Verified reproducer confirms the inconsistency between CLI and SDK behavior. Affects any SDK consumer using plugin-loaded agents.

source_issues.title: Options.agent silently falls back to default Claude for plugin-loaded agent names
source_issues.evidence: SDK uses wrong agent silently — CLI correctly resolves same name. Repro proves agent field works; only plugin-registry lookup is broken. Silent fallback is worst failure mode: no error, no warning, no log. Users receive wrong model with no indication of misconfiguration.

signals.topic: instance.interrupt() is flaky and does not reliably pause active sessions
signals.summary: Manual user pause via instance.interrupt() fails intermittently. In some sessions, interrupt() is called but never reaches the expected completion path — no 'interrupt() completed' log appears and the session does not pause. Logs show the call is made to an active session but the interrupt is silently ignored.
signals.review_reason: User abort/interrupt is a critical control-plane operation for production deployments. Flaky behavior means sessions cannot be reliably stopped — a core workflow blocker. Count=1 limits to P1 despite high severity. The provided logs provide concrete evidence of the intermittent failure.

source_issues.title: manual user pause is flaky
source_issues.evidence: Real logs comparing failed vs successful pause show interrupt() call made to active session but completion log never appears. Session remains unpaused after multiple abort attempts. Flaky behavior confirmed across multiple attempts with ~4 minute gap.

signals.topic: Claude Opus 4.7 missing from SDK hardcoded model registry, latest model unavailable via SDK
signals.summary: Claude Opus 4.7 has been GA since April 16, 2026 and is available across all other Anthropic platforms (API, Claude Code CLI, Claude.ai, Bedrock, Vertex AI, Foundry), but the SDK's hardcoded model registry only includes up to Opus 4.6. Users of the SDK cannot access the latest model.
aliases: latest model not in SDK registry
hardcoded model list out of date
signals.review_reason: Key functional gap: latest GA model inaccessible through SDK while available on all other platforms. Users must work around by using the API directly. Count=1 limits to P1 but the inconsistency across platforms is a real usability and feature parity issue.

source_issues.title: Claude Opus 4.7 missing from ACP model list (hardcoded model registry only includes up to Opus 4.6)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed via grep of SDK source (v0.2.131): claude-opus-4-7 is absent. CLI has Opus 4.7. Latest model on all other platforms but not in SDK.

signals.topic: Native installer reports success but binary is missing; action silently proceeds and fails downstream
signals.summary: The Claude Code installer emits 'successfully installed' messages while simultaneously warning the binary is not at the expected path. The action trusts the exit code without verifying the binary exists, causing downstream steps to fail with ENOENT.
signals.review_reason: Two independent regressions showing the same root cause: the action's install logic trusts the CLI exit code without verifying the binary exists. Both times the action fails silently downstream with ENOENT after emitting misleading success output. Clear user impact — broken installation blocks all downstream work.

source_issues.title: Native installer reports '✔ successfully installed' while emitting '⚠ claude command not found' warnings (v1.0.106 regression)
source_issues.evidence: Installer reports '✔ Claude Code successfully installed' and '✅ Installation complete!' while emitting '⚠ claude command not found at /home/runner/.local/bin/claude'; next step 'Adding marketplace' immediately ENOENT'd trying to invoke the non-existent binary.

source_issues.title: plugin_marketplaces fails: claude install exits 0 but binary not placed at ~/.local/bin/claude
source_issues.evidence: Same pattern recurred in v1.0.113 era. Installer exits 0, emits '✔ Claude Code successfully installed! Version: 2.1.129 Location: ~/.local/bin/claude' but binary is not present. Action then fails with 'ENOENT: no such file or directory, posix_spawn /home/runner/.local/bin/claude'.

signals.topic: Internal 'directory mismatch for tsconfig.json' error appears on every run, failing the workflow
signals.summary: An internal error about directory mismatch for the action's bundled tsconfig.json file occurs on every workflow run, causing the action to exit 1.
signals.review_reason: Two reports confirm this error blocks workflow runs (exit 1) on every invocation. The error itself indicates a bug in the action's internal file path handling. Consistent failure with no user workaround.

source_issues.title: Internal error: directory mismatch for '.../claude-code-action/<ref>/tsconfig.json', fd 4 — fails on every run
source_issues.evidence: Every triggered run logs 'Internal error: directory mismatch for directory /home/runner/work/_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action/<ref>/tsconfig.json' and returns exit 1. Affects both floating tag (@v1) and SHA-pinned refs. One earlier run succeeded, suggesting a regression that landed during 2026-04-26.

source_issues.title: Internal error: directory mismatch for tsconfig.json
source_issues.evidence: Same error pattern recurs: 'Internal error: directory mismatch for directory /home/runner/work/_actions/anthropics/claude-code-action/v1/tsconfig.json'. Error appears twice during run and again during post-run cleanup. Action still completes but logs are polluted.

signals.topic: Generated workflow template has insufficient permissions; action exits 0 even on 403 write failures
signals.summary: The workflow template generated by /install-github-app omits 'pull-requests: write'. When the action tries to post review comments with only 'read' permission it receives a 403, but the action exits 0, making the entire misconfiguration invisible.
signals.review_reason: Two compounding bugs: wrong template permissions + silent failure on 403. Users get a green workflow run with no output, making the failure invisible and requiring manual log inspection to diagnose.

source_issues.title: claude-code-review workflow template generates insufficient permissions; action silently swallows write failure
source_issues.evidence: Generated template sets 'pull-requests: read', but posting review comments requires 'pull-requests: write'. When the action receives a 403 from the GitHub API, it exits 0. Job shows green; reviews silently go nowhere.

signals.topic: Agent halts after Edit/Write phase with end_turn, never invoking Bash — multi-step prompts silently fail to complete
signals.summary: Agent reads files and makes Edits/Writes, then voluntarily halts with stop_reason: end_turn and empty result string, skipping all Bash invocations. Multi-step prompts that require Bash for verification, git ops, or PR creation fail silently.
signals.review_reason: Seven reproducible runs confirm a consistent main-flow failure: the agent voluntarily stops after Edit/Write without running Bash. Multi-step workflows silently produce no work product while reporting success. This is a primary flow blocker for automation use cases.

source_issues.title: Agent halts after Edit/Write phase with stop_reason: end_turn, never invokes Bash; multi-step prompts fail to complete (claude-sonnet-4-6)
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible across 7 runs in ~14 hours. Agent makes Edit/Write calls then halts with stop_reason: end_turn, result: '' (empty), is_error: false. 0 Bash invocations vs 42 in baseline. Pending TodoWrite items remain pending. Action returns outcome: success, making failure invisible to the orchestrating workflow.

signals.topic: claude-code-action uses GitHub App credentials bypassing workflow permissions; unexpected code pushes occur despite 'contents: read'
signals.summary: The action uses its own GitHub App credentials (granted at App install time) rather than the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN. Declaring 'permissions: contents: read' in the workflow YAML does not constrain the action from pushing commits.
signals.review_reason: Security-relevant UX failure: users cannot rely on workflow permissions to constrain the action's write behavior. Unexpected commits pushed to branches despite explicit read-only declarations. Primary trust/security concern for repo owners.

source_issues.title: claude-code-action pushes commits when only review was requested; workflow 'permissions: contents: read' does not constrain it
source_issues.evidence: Action made and pushed a commit to a PR branch under claude[bot] identity in response to a review-only request. Workflow YAML declared 'permissions: contents: read' but the action bypassed it by using GitHub App credentials. Users have no visible guardrail preventing unintended code pushes.

signals.topic: False-positive filter silently disabled — deprecated Haiku model causes 404 on every run, flooding PRs with unfiltered noise findings
signals.summary: The FP-filter step calls hardcoded deprecated model 'claude-3-5-haiku-20241022' which returns 404, silently disabling filtering on every run. All raw findings (including false positives) are posted as PR comments with no noise reduction.
aliases: Deprecated Haiku model breaks FP filter
Silent FP filter failure due to deprecated model
signals.review_reason: Clear user-visible workflow degradation: FP filter is silently disabled on every run (not intermittent), causing all raw findings including noise to be posted as PR comments. This directly pollutes developer PRs and undermines the action's core value proposition. Evidence includes actual error logs (404 for deprecated model) and concrete impact description. Excluded from P0 only because count=1 and single repo — priority bumped to P1 due to the continuous/every-run nature and clear degradation of the main user workflow.

source_issues.title: False-positive filter fails with 404: model 'claude-3-5-haiku-20241022' not found
source_issues.evidence: Claude API validation failed with 404: model claude-3-5-haiku-20241022 not found. FP filter silently disabled on every run. Every raw finding posted as PR comment with no noise filtering. Main scan completes but PRs flooded with false positives.

signals.topic: Git LFS not supported in Claude Code Web — proxy rejects LFS batch API
signals.summary: Repositories using Git LFS cannot pull LFS-tracked files in Claude Code Web, blocking the main development workflow
aliases: LFS file pull blocked in web
signals.review_reason: Git LFS is a standard tool for managing large binary files in development workflows. When LFS pull fails, the entire git workflow is blocked — users cannot retrieve large assets needed for their project. This is a primary development workflow failure, not a fringe scenario.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Claude Code on the Web: Git LFS not supported — proxy rejects LFS batch API with "invalid git path"
source_issues.evidence: Repositories that use Git LFS cannot pull LFS-tracked files in Claude Code Web. User explicitly notes this is a regression from a prior closed issue #25043.

signals.topic: HTTP MCP OAuth tokens stored in macOS Keychain but not loaded at session start — re-auth required every session
signals.summary: Valid OAuth tokens are written to Keychain but not read at startup, forcing manual re-authentication for all HTTP MCP servers on every Claude Code launch
aliases: HTTP MCP server always needs authentication
signals.review_reason: Multiple MCP servers across multiple users forced to re-authenticate on every single session despite valid tokens stored in Keychain. Issue author traced the root cause to the runtime not reading stored tokens — not a configuration issue. Six prior reports across Jan–May 2026 confirm this is a recurring systemic failure, not an isolated incident. Every new session requires manual re-auth, breaking the core MCP integration workflow.

source_issues.title: [BUG] HTTP MCP OAuth tokens written to macOS Keychain but not loaded at session start — re-auth required every session
source_issues.evidence: Issue author documents 6+ prior related issues (#16957, #20785, #21333, #25245, #27509, #47540) all closed without durable fix. 60+ sessions affected over 60+ days. Tokens confirmed in Keychain but runtime re-stamps mcp-needs-auth-cache.json on every start. Affects Notion, Glean, Linear, Vercel, Slack — multiple MCP servers. Silent failure (no log entries).

signals.topic: Effort level changes in one session affecting concurrent other sessions despite v2.1.133 fix
signals.summary: The /effort command in one session modifies effort level of other concurrent sessions, a regression of a previously fixed bug
signals.review_reason: Explicit regression of a previously acknowledged and supposedly fixed bug. Session state leaking between concurrent sessions corrupts per-session configuration. User loses independent control over effort levels across different projects/sessions simultaneously — a significant UX regression.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Effort level changes affecting concurrent sessions despite v2.1.133 fix
source_issues.evidence: Explicitly a regression: v2.1.133 was supposed to fix this exact issue, but as of v2.1.138 it is still broken. User confirms effort level changes in one session are bleeding into other concurrent sessions on the same machine.

signals.topic: Claude Code times out or responds very slowly on simple prompts on Windows
signals.summary: CLI hangs or times out on simple prompts on Windows, with feedback command also timing out, blocking all interaction
signals.review_reason: The main workflow (sending prompts and getting responses) is blocked on Windows — not slow, effectively broken. The fact that /feedback also times out means the user cannot even report the issue through the normal channel, compounding the impact. Web version working confirms this is a platform-specific regression.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Claude Code falls to timeout or answering very slow on simple prompts
source_issues.evidence: Haiku model took 1m 54s to respond to a simple prompt. User tried multiple fixes (reinstall npm, relogin, VS Code reload, Windows reload) — none worked. Web version works fine. Even /feedback command times out, leaving user with no way to report the issue. Complete workflow blockage on Windows.

signals.topic: Usage limit reached error shown despite 0% usage displayed in desktop app
signals.summary: Windows desktop app shows usage limit reached error with 0% usage across all limits, completely blocking the tool
aliases: Usage limit error with zero usage
Desktop app usage limit false positive
signals.review_reason: A paying Pro user cannot use Claude Code at all — the app claims limits are reached while showing 0% usage. This is a cost/billing discrepancy that renders the entire tool unusable. User has an active subscription and cannot access the product they paid for. Multiple troubleshooting attempts failed, and the desktop app is the primary interface for many users.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Usage limit reached error with 0% usage displayed
source_issues.evidence: Active Pro subscription user on Windows desktop app sees 'Limit reached' error immediately on first prompt, despite UI showing 0% usage across all limits. User exhausted all troubleshooting steps (3+ restarts, logout/login, different device, different models, 30+ min wait). Desktop app completely unusable. Screenshots confirm discrepancy.

signals.topic: hookify: field name mismatch (user_prompt vs prompt) causes all UserPromptSubmit rules to silently never match
signals.summary: Rules using field: user_prompt always return empty string because Claude Code's UserPromptSubmit payload key is 'prompt', not 'user_prompt'. All warn/block rules silently fail.
aliases: hookify prompt event rules never match
signals.review_reason: All hookify rules using field: user_prompt silently fail — the core gating mechanism of the hookify plugin is completely broken for every user who follows the documented field name. Four independent users/reporters confirm the issue across multiple days. The fix is confirmed and simple (accept both keys). This breaks the entire purpose of the plugin for UserPromptSubmit use cases.

source_issues.title: hookify: UserPromptSubmit rules with field: user_prompt never fire (wrong payload key)
source_issues.evidence: _extract_field in rule_engine.py reads input_data.get('user_prompt', '') but Claude Code's UserPromptSubmit payload uses key 'prompt'. Rule loads fine, event fires, but field value always resolves to empty string so no condition ever matches. Docs say field: user_prompt so users follow docs and rules silently do nothing.

source_issues.title: hookify: prompt rules never match — field name mismatch with UserPromptSubmit hook input
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed: UserPromptSubmit payload has 'prompt' key, not 'user_prompt'. _extract_field returns '' for every prompt rule. Reproduction: submit prompt containing 'hello' with field: user_prompt rule — rule never fires.

source_issues.title: [hookify] 4 fixes: Windows utf-8 / CC prompt key / global path / additionalContext (PR #1732 auto-closed)
source_issues.evidence: Issue #1738 bundles the same prompt key mismatch fix as part of 4 Windows fixes, independently discovered by a different user. Patch confirmed: change field == 'user_prompt' to 'user_prompt' or field == 'prompt' and return input_data.get('prompt') or input_data.get('user_prompt', '').

source_issues.title: hookify: action: block does not block UserPromptSubmit prompts
source_issues.evidence: Issue #1788 explicitly states that combined with the field-name bug, 'event: prompt rules currently don't work at all'. Same underlying field mismatch renders block rules ineffective.

signals.topic: Remember plugin: save-session.sh resolves PROJECT_DIR to plugin install dir, causing session memory files to never be written to user's project
signals.summary: save-session.sh hardcodes three-level relative path resolution, always writing to plugin cache dir instead of user's project. .remember/ now.md, today-*.md, recent.md, archive.md, core-memories.md are never created.
aliases: session memory files never saved to project
signals.review_reason: Critical data-loss-level bug: all Remember session memory files (now.md, today-*.md, recent.md, archive.md, core-memories.md) are NEVER created for any user in any project. Every user who relies on Remember for session continuity is silently losing all their memory. Root cause is confirmed in code. Affects every invocation of save-session.sh.

source_issues.title: remember: save-session.sh resolves PROJECT_DIR to plugin install dir, never to the user's project
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: script uses '$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../.." && pwd)' which always resolves to ~/.claude/plugins/cache/, not $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR. Files .remember/now.md, today-*.md, recent.md, archive.md, core-memories.md are never created. Workaround is to manually invoke /remember before each session end.

source_issues.title: claude-md-management: claude-md-improver skill not discovered — plugin.json missing skills path
source_issues.evidence: Same plugin.json schema issue: missing 'skills' field in plugin.json causes skill auto-discovery to fail silently. Confirmed the save-session.sh also has the same pattern of hardcoded paths diverging from env-var pattern used in other hooks in the same plugin.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin: silent multi-hour polling wedge due to unbounded grammy client timeout (500s default)
signals.summary: grammy's internal handlePollingError swallows all non-401/409 errors silently and retries forever. Combined with bun's half-open TCP behavior, bot can wedge for 34+ hours with no errors logged while inbound messages are silently lost.
aliases: Telegram inbound silently lost for hours
signals.review_reason: Critical communication outage: Telegram users who rely on the bridge for work communication go completely silent for 34+ hours with zero indication something is wrong. The process appears healthy, logs show nothing, but no messages get through. Two separate bridges wedged simultaneously, confirming it's a structural issue in the plugin, not an edge case. The silent-retry mechanism with no alerting means users cannot diagnose the problem without external monitoring.

source_issues.title: fix(telegram): cap grammy client.timeoutSeconds=90 to bound silent handlePollingError retries (multi-hour wedge)
source_issues.evidence: Two independent Telegram bridges wedged for 34+ hours. Process alive, TCP poll holding lease, but inbound updates never reach Claude Code. Root cause: grammy's handlePollingError silently swallows all non-401/409 errors (HttpError, ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT, AbortError, 5xx) — debugErr writes to DEBUG=grammy* channel which plugin doesn't set, so errors are invisible. Combined with bun half-open TCP behavior, recovery takes up to 500s per attempt. Fix: set timeoutSeconds=90, bounding wedge to ≤93s.

Since Nimble is listed in the official marketplace, users expect it to work correctly out of the box.

Ollama panic breaks local model inference entirely; DeepSeek 400 errors block multi-turn conversations with DeepSeek models; extra_body omission prevents use of provider-specific parameters like Mistral reasoning_effort. Together these break core local-model workflows and provider customization — a primary use case.

timeout: 300 in config overridden by 30s default across all sessions

signals.topic: SQLite foreign key enforcement disabled — thread deletion silently orphans associated rows
signals.summary: The SQLite connection pool never enables PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON, so all REFERENCES constraints in the schema are declared but never enforced. Deleting a thread leaves thread_messages rows orphaned without any error. This is a silent data integrity failure affecting session data correctness.
aliases: SQLite FK pragma not set in connection pool
thread_messages rows orphaned when thread deleted due to missing FK enforcement
Silent database integrity gap in SessionStorage SQLite pool
signals.review_reason: Silent data integrity failure: SQLite FK enforcement is disabled by default in the connection pool, causing thread_messages rows to be orphaned when threads are deleted — with no error or warning shown to the user. This corrupts session state data without any visible indication, and affects all FK constraints in the schema. Data integrity loss is a critical user impact even at count=1.

source_issues.title: SQLite foreign key enforcement disabled — thread_messages orphans on thread delete
source_issues.evidence: Connection pool in SessionStorage never sets PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON. thread_messages table has no ON DELETE CASCADE. Deleting a thread silently orphans associated thread_messages rows. Queries joining thread_messages to threads on deleted threads return stale data.

signals.review_reason: Two independent users on Windows with Chinese locales report the same root cause: shell output panel uses wrong encoding (CP936/GBK) for subprocess stdout, rendering non-ASCII output unreadable. source_issues.title: Autocomplete using Openrouter doesn't send extraBodyProperties

signals.topic: edit_existing_file silently fails in VS Code despite chat confirming success
signals.summary: The edit_existing_file tool sometimes does not apply changes to files even though the chat interface reports 'File edited successfully'. Users are misled by false success messages and must manually verify every edit, leading to confusion and potential missed changes.

signals.review_reason: Authentication failure for newly registered users is a complete workflow blockage for Continue Hub. Users cannot access any hub features after going through the signup process. This is a hard block on user onboarding for the hub service.

signals.topic: AWS Bedrock native function calling drops all tool arguments — every tool call fails with Pydantic validation error
signals.summary: When using AWS Bedrock as the LLM provider with native function calling, all tool arguments are silently dropped and replaced with empty dict {}. Every tool call fails with Pydantic 'Field required' or 'missing' errors, blocking all tool use for Bedrock users.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocker for all AWS Bedrock users with native function calling enabled. Every tool call fails immediately with Pydantic validation errors, rendering tool use completely non-functional for this provider. Reproducible with a one-line fix identified in the issue.

source_issues.title: [BUG] _parse_native_tool_call drops Bedrock Converse API tool arguments — always passes empty dict
source_issues.evidence: Every tool call fails with 'Field required [type=missing, input_value={}, input_type=dict]' on any tool with required parameters. Root cause: func_args = func_info.get('arguments', '{}') or tool_call.get('input', {}) — truthy default '{}' prevents fallthrough to Bedrock's 'input' field. Affects all Bedrock models using native function calling.

signals.topic: @persist decorator does not persist state across runs — documented behavior contradicts actual behavior
signals.summary: The @persist decorator documented in the official Flows documentation does not actually persist state between runs. The second run returns the same result as the first, rather than the expected cumulative result, making flow persistence non-functional.
signals.review_reason: This is a direct contradiction between documented behavior and actual behavior, causing persistent state to be non-functional. Users following the official documentation cannot achieve the expected persistence, blocking a core advertised feature. Low reproduction friction — just run the documented code twice.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Wrong code in document
source_issues.evidence: User ran the exact code from the official documentation (mastering-flow-state, class-level persistence). First run: result=2. Second run: result=2 (expected 4). The @persist decorator fails to carry state between executions, contradicting the documented behavior.

signals.topic: HITL pre-review with learn=True fails open silently — automated safeguards bypassed with no signal to caller
signals.summary: When @human_feedback(learn=True) is used and lessons are recalled, any exception during LLM pre-review (network, auth, LLM error, structured-output issues) is caught by a bare except and returns raw output. No exception propagates, no warning is logged, and callers cannot distinguish pre-reviewed output from raw output.
signals.review_reason: This causes automated safeguards in the HITL learn pipeline to be silently bypassed with no observable signal. Users relying on learn=True to improve their flows have no way to detect when pre-review fails, leading to degraded quality without awareness. The silent fallback without any logging or metadata is a significant observability gap.

source_issues.title: [BUG]: HITL pre-review fails open and silently bypasses automated safeguards
source_issues.evidence: Bare except block in _pre_review_with_lessons catches all exceptions and returns method_output (raw). No exception propagated, no warning/error logged. Downstream callers cannot detect whether pre-review actually ran. Violates documented 'graceful degradation' expectations.

signals.topic: crewai create CLI template contains eval() on LLM input — RCE risk in all new projects generated from template
signals.summary: The AGENTS.md template bundled with 'crewai create' project scaffolding includes a Calculator tool that uses eval() on LLM-provided input. Every new project following this template or leaving the example as-is is vulnerable to remote code execution via indirect prompt injection.
signals.review_reason: This is a shipped vulnerability in the official CLI template that affects every new CrewAI project. When agents process untrusted documents (the primary use case for LLM agents), the template's eval() pattern enables full host compromise via indirect prompt injection. The attack vector is realistic and well-documented in the issue. This is a systemic security defect, not a one-off user error.

source_issues.title: [Security] crewai create ships template with eval() on unsanitized LLM input
source_issues.evidence: Template file lib/crewai/src/crewai/cli/templates/AGENTS.md line 773: 'return str(eval(expression))'. An agent processing a malicious document can be tricked into calling calculator() with arbitrary Python code, executing it on the host system. Classified as ASI-09 / CWE-95. No sanitization or sandboxing.

signals.topic: CLI falls back to binary name as pattern when -p is omitted, producing misleading "pattern not found" error that blocks user workflows
signals.summary: When calling fabric-ai without -p flag but with positional args or -y/--transcript, the CLI erroneously falls back to os.Args[0] (binary name 'fabric-ai') as the pattern name, emitting a confusing error that sends users in the wrong debugging direction (e.g., misinterpreting as "not installed" or "Homebrew broken"). This is a regression from #1960 and blocks the documented README zsh yt() helper.

The error message is sufficiently confusing that users misdiagnose it as installation or packaging issues rather than a CLI logic regression. Reproducer confirmed, root cause identified (#1960), and fix direction clear (clearer error or correct default behavior). Impact is real and reproducible, not a theoretical concern.

signals.topic: Race condition in EditTool causes silent file content loss during parallel edit operations
signals.summary: When the scheduler executes parallel edits on the same file, concurrent read-modify-write operations clobber each other's changes with no warning. One operation's changes are permanently lost.
signals.review_reason: User work is silently lost with no error message when the agent performs parallel edits. The EditTool has no file locking mechanism, causing permanent data loss that users may not discover until much later. This is a data-integrity catastrophe for a coding agent.

signals.topic: Codex integration ignores 'never stop' instruction in interactive sessions, breaking continuous agent operation
signals.summary: Codex-based agents in autoresearch ignore instructions to never stop generation, causing premature termination in interactive sessions. This blocks the core use case of monitoring and pitching in to running agent tasks, unlike Claude-based sessions where the /loop feature works correctly.
signals.review_reason: This is a user pain point because it directly blocks the main interactive session workflow: users cannot maintain continuous Codex agent sessions, cannot monitor agent progress in real time, and cannot pitch in to running tasks. Unlike Claude which handles this correctly, Codex integration fails to respect the 'never stop' instruction, making the core interactive feature unusable with Codex. signals.topic: SkillsMiddleware fails to load skills on first agent turn due to empty-list guard bug

The guard `if 'skills_metadata' in state` fires on the empty list, preventing _list_skills_with_errors from ever running on the first turn. System prompt shows '(No skills available yet)' even when valid skills exist on disk.

signals.review_reason: Core agent functionality is broken on every user's first interaction. Skills that are explicitly configured are silently not loaded, making the agent appear to have no skills despite valid SKILL.md files on disk. The bug is deterministic (first turn always fails), reproducible across all backends, and the proposed fix is straightforward but the bug exists in production (0.5.7). Three independent reports confirm user impact.

signals.topic: Modal sandbox deploy template missing required app= parameter causes InvalidError on deployment
signals.summary: The bundler-generated deploy_graph.py calls modal.Sandbox.create(image=image) without the required app= argument. The modern Modal SDK (1.x+) raises InvalidError when Sandbox.create is called outside a Modal container without app=. This blocks the deploy workflow entirely for any user using Modal sandbox mode.
aliases: modal sandbox deployment failure missing app parameter
signals.review_reason: This is a deployment workflow blocker. Any user who runs `deepagents dev` with sandbox.provider='modal' gets an unhandled InvalidError crash on the first sandbox creation attempt. The Modal SDK 1.x introduced a breaking change that the deploy template does not account for. The crash is 100% reproducible for affected users and completely prevents the sandbox from functioning. Two independent reports confirm the issue.

source_issues.evidence: deepagents.toml with sandbox.provider='modal' and scope='thread' causes deploy_graph.py to call modal.Sandbox.create(image=image) without app=. Modal SDK 1.4.2 raises InvalidError: 'Sandboxes require an App when created outside of a Modal container.' Verified fix: patch SANDBOX_BLOCK_MODAL with App.lookup pattern. Root cause in deepagents_cli/deploy/templates.py:151.

source_issues.title: [deploy] Modal sandbox template missing app= parameter — Sandbox.create raises InvalidError outside Modal container

signals.topic: read_file tool description examples use wrong kwarg name causing model validation errors and wasted LLM turns
signals.summary: READ_FILE_TOOL_DESCRIPTION in FilesystemMiddleware shows three worked examples using path= as the kwarg, but the tool schema declares the field as file_path. Models follow the description examples literally, emit read_file(path=...) and trip Pydantic validation with 'Field required: file_path', wasting an LLM turn on every file read attempt.
signals.review_reason: Every read_file tool invocation by any agent built with create_deep_agent and FilesystemMiddleware fails on the first attempt due to a kwarg mismatch between the description (which models read) and the schema (which validates). This causes a wasted LLM turn on every single file read, accumulating significant token waste across sessions. The bug spans all released versions, making it a pervasive issue for all FilesystemMiddleware users.

source_issues.title: FilesystemMiddleware: `read_file` description shows examples with wrong kwarg name (`path` vs schema's `file_path`)
source_issues.evidence: Schema correctly declares 'file_path' but description examples use 'path' in 3 out of 4 call-site examples. Models trained on the description emit read_file(path=...) and trigger 'Field required: file_path' Pydantic validation error. Every file read attempt wastes an LLM turn. Reproducible on 0.4.1, 0.4.12, 0.5.7, 0.6.0a1, and main. Fix is a 3-line description patch.

source_issues.title: FilesystemMiddleware: read_file description shows examples with wrong kwarg name (`path` vs schema's `file_path`)
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #3188. Confirmed across all released versions. Agent built via create_deep_agent against Claude Opus 4.7 reproducibly produces 'Error invoking tool read_file with kwargs {path: ...} with error: file_path: Field required' on every read attempt.

signals.topic: execute tool hardcodes status='success' on non-zero exit code causing agent retry spirals and massive token waste
signals.summary: FilesystemMiddleware's execute tool always returns ToolMessage with status='success' regardless of exit code. Failed commands (exit_code != 0) show as successful in LangSmith traces and agents cannot distinguish success from failure at the ToolMessage level, causing them to retry failed commands indefinitely.
aliases: command failure not detected by agent
signals.review_reason: Despite count=1, this is P0 because of documented massive token waste in production (8.8M tokens, 638 LLM turns on a single failure event). The execute tool is a core FilesystemMiddleware tool used in every agent session. When commands fail, the agent cannot detect failure and enters an infinite retry spiral. This directly causes significant financial cost (LLM token billing) and completely blocks the agent's ability to self-correct on command failures.

source_issues.title: execute tool hardcodes status='success' on non-zero exit code
source_issues.evidence: PRODUCTION INCIDENT: FileNotFoundError on every execute call caused agent to spiral for 638 LLM turns / 8.8M tokens because status='success' gave no signal to stop retrying. LangSmith traces show failed commands as 'success', making error filtering impossible. Located in deepagents/middleware/filesystem.py sync_execute and async_execute around line 1535/1624.

signals.topic: CLI agent enables unsandboxed arbitrary shell command execution on host system via LocalShellBackend
signals.summary: deepagents_cli uses LocalShellBackend by default when sandbox=None, giving the agent an execute tool that runs arbitrary shell commands directly on the host OS with full user privileges. With --auto-approve and --shell-allow-list all flags, any prompt can trigger arbitrary command execution, enabling full filesystem access, data exfiltration, and system compromise.
signals.review_reason: This is a security vulnerability with clear user impact — arbitrary shell command execution on the host system. However, it requires explicit user flags (--auto-approve + --shell-allow-list all), so it is not a silent default that affects all users. The vulnerability is real and exploitable, but the attack surface requires intentional misconfiguration. Classified as P1 rather than P0 due to the explicit opt-in requirement.

source_issues.title: Unsandboxed Code Execution via LocalShellBackend in CLI Agent
source_issues.evidence: Root cause in libs/cli/deepagents_cli/agent.py lines 1178-1195: create_cli_agent() uses LocalShellBackend when sandbox=None (default). Combined with --auto-approve, the agent executes arbitrary shell commands on the host system. Attack scenarios include arbitrary file write (echo PWNED > /tmp/exploit.txt), data exfiltration via curl, and full system access. No sandboxing applied by default. Works on Linux, macOS, Windows.

signals.topic: SSRF security bypass in validate_safe_url via LANGCHAIN_ENV=local_test environment variable
signals.summary: validate_safe_url in langchain-core contains a raw-return bypass that skips all SSRF validation when LANGCHAIN_ENV=local_test and hostname matches startswith('test') and 'server' in hostname. Attacker-controlled hostnames like test.attacker.server.com bypass scheme, private-IP, and cloud-metadata checks entirely. Additionally, _effective_allowed_hosts() uses startswith('local') expanding the allowlist to any env var prefixed with 'local'.
aliases: SSRF bypass via test environment variable
signals.review_reason: Two independent duplicate reports confirm an exploitable SSRF bypass where attacker-controlled hostnames completely bypass all SSRF protection (scheme, private-IP, cloud-metadata checks) when LANGCHAIN_ENV=local_test. This is a critical security vulnerability — any user with control over the LANGCHAIN_ENV variable in a shared or test environment can weaponize LangChain to perform SSRF attacks against internal/cloud metadata endpoints.

source_issues.title: Bug: SSRF bypass in validate_safe_url when LANGCHAIN_ENV=local_test
source_issues.evidence: validate_safe_url('http://test.attacker.server.com/exfil') returns URL unchecked when LANGCHAIN_ENV=local_test. Reproduction code provided.

source_issues.title: Bug: exploitable SSRF bypass in validate_safe_url via LANGCHAIN_ENV=local_test

Any caller with access to the public API can read arbitrary files from the filesystem including sensitive system files, returning content base64-encoded through the embeddings pipeline.

signals.review_reason: Two independent duplicate reports confirm a path traversal vulnerability where the public Chroma.add_images() API reads arbitrary files from the filesystem with no path validation. Any user calling this API can read /etc/passwd and other sensitive files. This is a file-system arbitrary-read vulnerability in a widely-used vector store integration.

source_issues.title: Bug: path traversal in Chroma.add_images() via unsanitized URI
source_issues.evidence: Identical path traversal vulnerability reported independently. URIs parameter is part of public API accepting any caller-supplied string. Closed as duplicate.

signals.topic: SQL agent tutorial: interrupt branch unreachable when using stream_mode='values' due to conditional ordering
signals.summary: In the official LangGraph SQL agent tutorial code, the if 'messages' in step check always runs first, preventing the elif '__interrupt__' branch from ever executing. When the graph reaches an interrupt, the streamed step contains both 'messages' and '__interrupt__', so the interrupt handler is unreachable.
aliases: LangGraph SQL agent tutorial interrupt unreachable
signals.review_reason: A documentation code bug in the official SQL agent tutorial: the interrupt handling branch is unreachable because stream_mode='values' returns both 'messages' and '__interrupt__' in the same step, causing the first conditional to always match. This misleads developers following the tutorial and prevents them from understanding how to handle agent interrupts — a key LangGraph feature.

source_issues.title: A bug in learn-langgraph-SQL-agent
source_issues.evidence: Tutorial code at docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/sql-agent#4-define-application-steps has incorrect conditional ordering. The step dict contains both 'messages' and '__interrupt__' simultaneously, so if 'messages' in step: always matches first, making the elif branch unreachable. User cannot see interrupt details.

signals.topic: Checkpoint serialization produces massive storage bloat (85%) and token overhead (37.8%) across all checkpointers — no pluggable serializer exists
signals.summary: LangGraph's BaseCheckpointSaver uses full Pydantic metadata serialization (dumpd) on every checkpoint write. A 16-turn ReAct agent (65 messages) produces 21,850 bytes vs 3,217 with a compact serializer (85.3% overhead). LLM context token overhead is 37.8% per call. No SerializerProtocol or opt-out path exists — users cannot plug in alternative serializers without forking internals. Author quantifies annual cost impact at $372,600 (48.8%) for a 10M-loop/year deployment at GPT-4o pricing.
aliases: Pydantic metadata overhead in checkpoint writes
signals.review_reason: Measurable 85% storage overhead and 37.8% token overhead compound on every checkpoint write and every LLM call across all checkpointers (MemorySaver, SqliteSaver, PostgresSaver). No escape hatch exists. Author provides reproducible benchmarks with tiktoken and quantifies financial impact ($372,600/year savings). This is a clear, compounding cost loss affecting every LangGraph deployment that uses checkpointing.

source_issues.title: LangGraph checkpoint serialization produces 85% storage bloat and 37.8% token overhead with no opt-out path - reproducible with drop-in fix
source_issues.evidence: Author provides tiktoken benchmarks: 16-turn agent checkpoint = 21,850 bytes native vs 3,217 bytes with extension (85.3% reduction). LLM context: 5,764 tokens vs 3,587 (37.8% overhead). Annual cost projection: $764,200 -> $391,600 at 10M loops/year (GPT-4o pricing). Drop-in extension available at makroumi/ulmen demonstrating fix viability.

signals.topic: Long tool calls (3–10 minutes) silently re-executed on LangGraph Cloud — causes 2–3x duplicate LLM calls and compute cost

Both complete successfully, producing 2–3x redundant work. Multiple workarounds attempted (BG_JOB_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_PERIOD_SECS=900, BG_JOB_ISOLATED_LOOPS=true, asyncio.to_thread wrapping) all failed. Related to BG_JOB_HEARTBEAT=120 hardcoded and Runs.Sweep() re-queuing cancelled runs as retriable.
aliases: Long-running tool re-dispatched from checkpoint on cloud
CancelledError re-queues runs causing duplicate work
signals.review_reason: Main workflow failure on LangGraph Cloud: long tool calls (3–10 min, legitimate agent use case) silently duplicate, resulting in 2–3x redundant LLM calls and compute. User identifies root cause in langgraph-api source (CancelledError treated as retriable, BG_JOB_HEARTBEAT hardcoded). Source analysis shows CancelledError is marked ALL_RETRIABLE_EXCEPTIONS in langgraph-api, causing swept runs to return to pending and re-dispatch.

signals.topic: langgraph dev port binding fails for ~60 seconds after Ctrl+C due to TCP TIME-WAIT — blocks developer restart workflow
signals.summary: After stopping 'langgraph dev' with Ctrl+C, restarting immediately fails with 'OSError: Port 2024 is already in use' for ~60 seconds. No process is actually LISTEN-ing — the error is caused by TCP TIME-WAIT socket state. The only workaround is waiting or rebooting. Root cause: _resolve_port() in langgraph_api/cli.py uses a bind attempt to check availability without SO_REUSEADDR, so TIME-WAIT entries trigger false positives.
aliases: langgraph dev port 2024 TIME-WAIT false positive
OSError port in use after Ctrl+C restart
signals.review_reason: Primary development workflow blocking: 'langgraph dev' cannot be restarted immediately after Ctrl+C for ~60 seconds despite no actual port conflict. Blocks the core iterative dev loop. Root cause (TCP TIME-WAIT without SO_REUSEADDR) is clearly identified, reproducible by design, and fix is trivial. Affects every developer using 'langgraph dev'.

source_issues.title: langgraph dev falsely reports 'Port 2024 already in use' due to TIME-WAIT entries
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with: (1) run 'langgraph dev', (2) connect via studio/agent-chat-ui, (3) Ctrl+C to stop, (4) restart immediately -> OSError. No LISTEN-ing process exists. User provides root cause analysis and a one-line fix (add SO_REUSEADDR before bind). The 60-second window blocks the primary developer restart workflow.

signals.topic: PostgresStore numeric filter operators ($gt/$gte/$lt/$lte) use lexicographic (text) comparison — silently returns wrong query results
signals.summary: PostgresStore._get_filter_condition() uses PostgreSQL 'value->>key' (TEXT extraction) with string-cast parameters for $gt/$gte/$lt/$lte operators. In PostgreSQL, '9' >= '10' is True in text ordering. This means filter={"score": {"$gte": 10}} incorrectly includes items with score=2..9. The same bug does not exist in SqliteStore (which uses CAST(...AS REAL)), indicating the fix was not propagated.
aliases: TEXT comparison instead of numeric in PostgresStore
signals.review_reason: Silent wrong results in production: numeric range filters ($gte/$gt/$lt/$lte) in PostgresStore produce incorrect query results because text comparison is used instead of numeric. Items that should be excluded are silently included. This is a data correctness failure in a database query layer, potentially corrupting application decisions in production.

source_issues.title: Bug: PostgresStore numeric filter operators ($gt, $gte, $lt, $lte) use lexicographic (text) comparison instead of numeric comparison
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows: $gte with value=10 produces SQL 'value->>%s >= %s' with params=['score', '10'], causing '9' >= '10' in text ordering. Items with score 2-9 incorrectly pass the filter. SqliteStore already handles this correctly with CAST(...AS REAL), confirming the bug is in the Postgres implementation specifically.

signals.topic: ensure_config mutates shared base config metadata — thread_id from one invocation leaks into all subsequent invocations
signals.summary: When using langchain >= 1.2.13 with langgraph and langchain's create_agent (which sets shared metadata {"ls_integration": "langchain_create_agent"}), ensure_config() assigns the metadata dict by reference without calling .copy(). This means configurable values like thread_id from one invocation get injected into the shared base config metadata. After the first invocation, all subsequent calls see leaked thread_id values, contaminating all future calls.
signals.review_reason: Cross-invocation state contamination: ensure_config() mutates the shared base config's metadata dict by reference, causing thread_id from one invocation to leak into all subsequent invocations. This breaks the langchain>=1.2.13 create_agent integration by causing data from prior threads to contaminate future thread executions.

source_issues.title: bug: ensure_config mutates shared metadata when copiable keys passed by reference
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction: after calling ensure_config(original_config, new_config), original_config.metadata is mutated — thread_id from new_config.configurable leaks into original_config.metadata. The shared dict is the base config set by langchain>=1.2.13's create_agent, so all subsequent invocations are contaminated with previous thread_id values.

signals.topic: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor unsandboxed code execution — arbitrary code runs without security controls
signals.summary: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor writes LLM-generated code to disk and executes it as a subprocess with no sandboxing, filesystem isolation, or network restrictions. Only a UserWarning is emitted at init, which is easily suppressed in production.
signals.review_reason: High-severity unsandboxed execution vulnerability enabling full system compromise. LLM-generated code is written to disk and executed directly with full host privileges via subprocess, with only a UserWarning as the safeguard. The warning is easily suppressed in production environments (-W ignore flag, logging pipelines), making this a latent but real risk for any user following quickstart examples. Matches OWASP Agentic Security Index ASI-09. Count=1 but P0 due to extreme severity (system-level compromise) and prevalence (LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor is the default code executor in many examples).

source_issues.title: [Security] LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing
source_issues.evidence: Full system compromise via arbitrary code execution with host privileges. Credential theft (SSH keys, cloud credentials). The only safeguard is a UserWarning at construction that can be silently swallowed in production (e.g., -W ignore, logging pipelines). OWASP ASI-09 Improper Output Handling, CWE-94. 14 comments indicating community awareness.

signals.topic: CLI update prompt design flaw causes users to accidentally install malicious npm packages globally

signals.topic: Windows app-server taskkill stdout leak corrupts JSONL output on non-English locales, breaking downstream consumers
signals.summary: On Windows with non-English system locale (e.g. zh-TW/CP-950), the codex app-server spawns taskkill to clean up failed MCP child processes, but taskkill's localized stdout text leaks onto codex's own stdout stream. On non-ASCII locales this produces non-UTF8 bytes that corrupt any JSONL consumer parsing app-server output. Downstream tools (e.g. codex-plugin-cc) detect non-JSON lines and tear down connections, making the entire plugin ecosystem unreliable on non-English Windows.
aliases: taskkill localized output corrupts JSONL Windows
app-server JSONL stream corruption non-English locale
Windows MCP cleanup stdout leak JSONL corruption
signals.review_reason: Reliability failure for the entire plugin/embedding ecosystem on non-English Windows: JSONL output stream is corrupted deterministically whenever an MCP server fails to start. Explicitly documented downstream impact on codex-plugin-cc and any other consumer parsing app-server stdout. Concrete byte-level evidence and identified cleanup code path.

source_issues.title: Windows: codex app-server leaks taskkill stdout into its own stdout (corrupts JSONL on non-English locales)
source_issues.evidence: Precise byte-level evidence: taskkill zh-TW output hex a6a8a55c3a20... corrupts stdout JSONL stream. Timestamps show leak fires exactly when codex gives up on failed MCP server and spawns taskkill /T /F /PID. Downstream codex-plugin-cc tears down connection with 'Unexpected token' parse error. Root cause: Stdio not set to null when spawning taskkill on Windows cleanup path.

signals.topic: Realtime session blocks on close and leaves unknown tool calls unresolved
signals.summary: RealtimeSession.close() does not wake consumers blocked on the event queue (#3284), causing async iteration to hang indefinitely. signals.topic: Streaming guardrail exceptions are swallowed, allowing runs to complete despite guardrail failures
signals.summary: In streaming runs, _run_output_guardrails_for_stream() catches ordinary output guardrail exceptions, logs them, and returns an empty list (#3280). The stream then completes and stores final_output as if the guardrail passed. Additionally, run_input_guardrails_with_queue() cancels sibling tasks but does not await them, leaving cleanup running after the exception has propagated.
aliases: Input guardrail queue leaves cancelled tasks unawaited
signals.review_reason: Streaming runs can complete and return is_complete=True despite an output guardrail having raised an exception. This defeats the purpose of guardrails as a safety mechanism — users believe their output passed checks when it did not. Repro shows final_output stored after guardrail failure. Direct user impact on safety-critical flows.

source_issues.title: Streaming guardrail exceptions can be swallowed or leave cancelled siblings unawaited
source_issues.evidence: _run_output_guardrails_for_stream logs and returns [] on ordinary output guardrail exception; streamed run completes with is_complete=True and stores final_output; callers have no signal the guardrail failed; cleanup_finished=False immediately after the exception propagates, confirming unawaited cancellation

signals.topic: Session pop_item misreports state after dropping corrupted newest entry
signals.summary: Non-MongoDB session backends (SQLite, AsyncSQLite, Redis, SQLAlchemy, Dapr) remove the newest item before deserializing it (#3304). If that newest item is corrupted, pop_item returns None even when older valid session history still exists. Callers interpret None as an empty session and stop trimming or rewinding, while valid history remains in the backend.
aliases: Session pop_item returns None with valid history remaining
Session backend corrupts state on newest item drop
signals.review_reason: Session state is misreported as empty when a single corrupted newest entry exists — valid history is hidden from callers. This directly breaks session management flows that rely on pop_item. Affects all non-MongoDB backends (SQLite, Redis, SQLAlchemy, Dapr). MongoDB was already fixed separately in PR #3247, confirming the severity.

source_issues.title: Session pop_item can report empty after dropping corrupt newest item

signals.topic: Streaming `accumulate_delta` drops tool_call fragments when first chunk contains duplicate index entries
signals.summary: When the first streaming chunk contains multiple `tool_calls` entries with the same `index`, `accumulate_delta` stores them as separate list elements instead of merging by logical index. Subsequent chunks merge into only the first entry, leaving an orphaned entry. The reconstructed `tool_calls[0].function.arguments` ends up broken and unparseable as JSON, making tool call execution fail silently.
aliases: streaming tool_calls delta accumulation broken for duplicate indexes
tool_calls index merge bug in first chunk

Confirmed root cause in `_deltas.py` early-return branches that skip index-merge logic on first chunk. Not blocking all users but causes silent tool_call failures.

streaming accumulator missing null guard for item field

signals.topic: Async Responses structured outputs parsing causes unbounded memory leak leading to OOM
signals.summary: AsyncResponses.parse() calls `construct_type_unchecked` with TypeVar-subscripted generics (`ParsedResponse[TextFormatT]`). Pydantic cannot resolve free TypeVars, so model_rebuild always fails and a new SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer (heavy Rust objects) is allocated on every single parse() call. In long-running servers, RSS grows linearly until OOM.
aliases: structured outputs parse memory leak unbounded SchemaValidator allocation
AsyncResponses parse OOM due to Pydantic TypeVar rebuild failure
signals.review_reason: Production OOM in long-running async servers. Flame graph confirms linear memory growth tied to repeated parse() calls. Root cause traced to Pydantic TypeVar resolution failure in the parsing layer. This is a critical resource leak that will eventually crash any server using structured outputs.

source_issues.title: Async Responses Structured Outputs Memory leak
source_issues.evidence: Flame graph attached showing unbounded growth. Root cause identified: TextFormatT TypeVar unresolved → model_rebuild fails → cache miss → new SchemaValidator per call. Fix: use non-parameterized base classes (Pars edResponse, ParsedResponseOutputText, ParsedResponseOutputMessage).

signals.topic: Static analyzer produces high-volume false positive security flags across multiple rule types
signals.summary: The ClawHub static analysis scanner generates systematic false positive flags across multiple rule families (env_credential_access, exposed_secret_literal, potential_exfiltration, obfuscated_code), causing significant friction for publishers. Affected rules flag env var reads as credential exfiltration, variable names as hardcoded secrets, base64-encoded platform API login parameters as exfiltration, library obfuscation as malicious code, and documentation content as executable patterns.
signals.review_reason: 7 distinct appeals across multiple rule families (env_credential_access, exposed_secret_literal, potential_exfiltration, obfuscated_code) all demonstrating the same root cause: scanner pattern-matching heuristics that cannot distinguish safe code patterns from malicious ones. While installs are non-blocking, the volume and cross-rule nature (>=3 distinct rules) confirm a systemic false-positive class that causes repeated review cycles, publication delays, and blocked discovery for legitimate publishers. Not P0 because verdict does not block installation.

signals.topic: Defensive-scanner skills are flagged for containing the patterns they scan for
signals.summary: Skills whose purpose is to scan other skills for malicious patterns are structurally guaranteed to be flagged by the same static analysis rules they are designed to detect. This is an architectural paradox: eval() in a PATTERNS array, prompt injection markers in SKILL.md documentation, and other defensive patterns all trigger the same rules that would catch the real threats. Rescan against newer engine (v2.4.22) made it worse by adding new LLM heuristic flags.
signals.review_reason: Architectural paradox: any defensive-scanner skill is structurally guaranteed to trip the scanner. This blocks legitimate security tooling from the platform. Engine upgrade (v2.4.22) made it worse by adding new LLM heuristic false positives. Provides five concrete remediation paths. Count=1 limits to P1 but the architectural nature makes it high priority.
