signals.topic: context-restore --confirm silently auto-approves in non-interactive agent environments
signals.summary: The alexunitario-sketch/context-restore skill's --confirm flag uses input() with an except block that silently sets confirmation='y' when EOFError occurs (in CI/CD, cron, LLM agent environments). The confirmation mechanism provides zero protection in the skill's primary use case (agent workflows). SKILL.md documents it as a gating feature, creating a documentation mismatch.
signals.review_reason: Real security concern: --confirm flag provides false sense of safety in agent environments. In non-interactive contexts (LLM agents, CI/CD, cron), confirmation silently passes. The skill is designed for agent workflows where this is the primary execution environment. Documentation mismatch amplifies the risk of unintended execution.

source_issues.title: Security: Skill context-restore fallback bypass user confirmation
source_issues.evidence: When input() raises EOFError in non-interactive mode, confirmation is silently set to 'y'. The skill is designed for agent workflows where non-interactive execution is the norm, making the confirmation mechanism a no-op.

signals.topic: WSL gateway onboarding validation fails — credential contamination and operator pairing auth errors block main flow
signals.summary: The WSL local gateway onboarding flow fails validation due to an environment variable isolation bug: the validation harness sets OPENCLAW_TRAY_APPDATA_DIR/LOCALAPPDATA_DIR but SettingsManager reads OPENCLAW_TRAY_DATA_DIR, causing the real user settings file to be touched with stale credentials. This leads to operator authentication failure (operator_auth_failed) after gateway start, blocking the entire onboarding flow. Multiple sub-issues compound: stale tray executable launched, token redaction gaps exposing secrets, weak wsl.conf section-aware checks, cancellation leaving processes running, and legacy DeviceToken vs NodeDeviceToken mismatches.
aliases: WSL gateway onboarding blocked by credential contamination
Operator pairing fails in WSL local gateway setup
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow onboarding failure: the WSL gateway setup is entirely blocked because credentials are contaminated across real/isolated settings. The issue has concrete error output ('operator_auth_failed'), clear root cause (wrong env var name), and 8 compounding sub-problems. It directly prevents users from completing local gateway setup, a core use case.

source_issues.title: WSL local gateway onboarding validation blockers from PR #274
source_issues.evidence: Validation harness wrote to real user settings file instead of isolated run folder due to wrong env var (APPDATA_DIR vs DATA_DIR), causing operator_auth_failed at PairOperator step. Gateway service running but root CLI context has no gateway auth. Stale Token overwrote BootstrapToken in contaminated settings.

signals.topic: Quick Send dialog titlebar ignores dark mode and blocks tray menu interaction
signals.summary: The Quick Send dialog does not use the custom titlebar (AppWindow.TitleBar.ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar), causing two distinct user-impacting problems: (1) titlebar shows light/mismatched styling instead of dark mode in dark theme, creating visual inconsistency across the app; (2) the dialog stays on top of z-order and does not light-dismiss, preventing users from opening the tray right-click menu flyout while Quick Send is open — the flyout immediately dismisses because focus returns to the dialog, forcing users to manually press Escape or click Cancel.
aliases: Quick Send dialog z-order blocks tray menu
Quick Send titlebar dark mode inconsistency
signals.review_reason: This is a UX regression that disrupts core tray interaction: the Quick Send dialog's focus/z-order behavior actively blocks users from accessing the tray context menu, a primary navigation surface. Combined with dark-mode titlebar inconsistency, this degrades daily usability. Not P0 because it doesn't fully block main workflow (Quick Send still works), just makes tray interaction awkward.

source_issues.title: Quick Send dialog: titlebar styling mismatch, focus/z-order issues
source_issues.evidence: User cannot open tray right-click menu while Quick Send is open; flyout immediately dismisses because focus returns to Quick Send dialog. Only dismissal path is manual Escape or Cancel click. Titlebar uses system default instead of custom 48px dark-mode-aware titlebar.

signals.topic: Tray menu flyout renders squished after display scaling change
signals.summary: When Windows display scaling is changed while the tray app is running, the right-click context menu renders squished/compressed on its first open after the DPI change. The second open renders correctly. Root cause: TrayMenuWindow is created once at startup and reused across DPI changes; SizeToContent() calls MenuPanel.Measure() with stale layout values from the previous DPI before XAML re-renders at the new scale.
aliases: DPI scaling causes tray menu to render incorrectly
TrayMenuWindow layout stale after DPI change
signals.review_reason: This is a visual rendering bug that causes a temporary but noticeable UI distortion after a common OS operation (changing display scaling). It is recoverable (second open is correct) and only triggered by a specific multi-step interaction, so P2. The root cause is well-identified but the impact is limited to a narrow window of time.

source_issues.title: Tray menu flyout renders squished after display scaling change until dismissed and reopened
source_issues.evidence: Repro steps provided: change Windows display scaling (100%->125%) while tray app running, first menu open is squished/compressed. Second open is correct. Confirmed root cause: SizeToContent() uses stale layout values before XAML re-renders.

signals.topic: Chat textbox does not auto-focus on window open, requiring extra click
signals.summary: When opening the chat window via tray icon left-click or context menu, the chat textbox does not receive keyboard focus automatically. Users must manually click into the textbox before typing. ShowNearTray() calls SetForegroundWindow but omits Focus() on the chat input element.
aliases: Chat window keyboard focus missing on open
signals.review_reason: Minor UX friction that causes an extra click on every chat window open. Not blocking but causes cumulative time waste. Well-scoped bug with clear root cause and fix. P2 given single-occurrence, recoverable behavior.

source_issues.title: Chat textbox should auto-focus when window opens
source_issues.evidence: Repro steps: click tray icon to open chat, try typing immediately, nothing happens. Must click textbox manually. Root cause identified: ShowNearTray() calls SetForegroundWindow but no Focus() call on input element.

signals.topic: Multiple AI provider integrations broken due to TLS errors, cached bad endpoints, or API protocol mismatches
signals.summary: Several AI provider integrations are completely broken: Kimi Code fails due to Node.js TLS stack incompatibility with api.kimi.com plus a cached broken endpoint; OpenRouter deepseek-v4-flash returns 400 due to sending both reasoning_effort and reasoning.effort fields; GitHub Copilot image tool is routed as copilot-language-server causing token exchange failure and 400; xai/grok-4.3 works via direct API but times out in the agent pipeline. Each of these represents a provider-specific protocol bug preventing users from using these models.
signals.review_reason: 4个独立provider集成均阻断特定模型使用，用户无法切换到免费/低成本替代方案。其中Kimi/OpenRouter/Copilot是明确API错误（400），grok-4.3是pipeline层超时。影响明确但非全量用户，P1。

source_issues.evidence: Node.js TLS stack incompatible with api.kimi.com; broken endpoint cached in config. Kimi Code integration unusable.

source_issues.title: xai/grok-4.3 idle timeout in agent pipeline
source_issues.evidence: Works via direct API but times out in agent pipeline; routing layer issue.

signals.topic: Exec policy shows security=full but commands are blocked with SYSTEM_RUN_DISABLED
signals.summary: Despite the effective exec policy explicitly displaying security=full and the host configured for full access, any shell command execution is denied with SYSTEM_RUN_DISABLED and security=deny. The system shows the correct policy but refuses execution — a regression blocking the primary agent execution workflow. No workaround exists; users must fall back to web search for workflows requiring shell commands.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: SYSTEM_RUN_DISABLED despite effective exec policy showing security=full
source_issues.evidence: Regression: exec denied (security=deny) despite effectivePolicy showing security=full. Reproduced on 2026.4.26 and 2026.5.7 across multiple gateway restarts. No workaround.

signals.topic: Cron jobs silently fall back to Opus model when configured model is rejected, causing unexpected cost surge
signals.summary: When a cron job payload.model is rejected by the provider, the system silently routes the job to the Opus model as a fallback without any notification to the user. The Apr 27 incident directly caused $50+ in unexpected billing. Users have no way to detect this silent routing — it only surfaces when users notice inflated costs on their billing statements.

opaque cost escalation on rejected models

source_issues.title: cron silently routes to Opus when payload.model is rejected
source_issues.evidence: Cron silently falls back to Opus when configured model is rejected; Apr 27 incident caused $50+ burn. No user notification, no error surfacing.

signals.topic: In-process gateway restart silently overwrites user config with stale snapshot
signals.summary: When a gateway is restarted in-process (e.g., via SIGUSR1), it reads a stale startupConfigSnapshotRead that overwrites the current user configuration. Every in-process restart in containerized deployments causes complete loss of user settings with no warning. This is particularly severe for production deployments where restarts happen frequently.
aliases: stale config snapshot overwrites user settings
signals.review_reason: 容器部署中每次in-process重启都会静默丢失用户配置，主流程阻断+数据丢失，用户无感知。P0条件满足。

source_issues.title: in-process gateway restart silently drops user config
source_issues.evidence: Stale startupConfigSnapshotRead overwrites user config on every SIGUSR1 restart in containers. Config is silently dropped — no warning, no recovery.

signals.topic: Browser plugin stale SingletonLock triggers OOM cascade that forces host reboot
signals.summary: The browser plugin holds a stale SingletonLock file that prevents proper Chrome instance management. Over a 6-hour period, 397 failed Chrome spawn attempts accumulated, consuming 2.5GB of RSS memory. This triggers an OOM cascade that kills gnome-shell, pipewire, and dbus, forcing the host machine to reboot. The user loses their entire desktop session.

signals.topic: Uncaught OSError crashes in pathlib path resolution when command-line arguments exceed path length limits
signals.summary: When system prompts or arguments exceed OS path length limits, the app crashes with uncaught OSError in pathlib.py stat() calls on startup, affecting Windows/macOS/Linux
aliases: OSError errno 36 errno 63 pathlib stat crash
signals.review_reason: Three uncaught OSError exceptions across Windows/macOS/Linux all triggered by the same root cause: long command-line arguments (--system-prompt, --extra-system-prompt) exceeding OS path length limits are passed to pathlib.Path().is_dir() which calls os.stat(), causing startup crashes. The app is completely blocked — it cannot even start. These are production-blocking crashes with clear user impact across multiple platforms.

source_issues.evidence: Linux crash: OSError [Errno 36] File name too long triggered by --extra-system-prompt argument during startup Path().is_dir() check

signals.topic: Edit-block path doubling causes files to be written to wrong paths and creates 0-byte stubs, risking data loss
signals.summary: Small/weak models (groq/llama, gpt-oss, gemini-flash-lite) emit edit-block filename headers with doubled directory prefixes, causing files to be written to wrong paths (e.g. .claude/.claude/foo.json) and canonical files to become 0-byte stubs
signals.review_reason: Model emits doubled directory prefix in edit-block header (e.g. .claude/.claude/foo.json instead of .claude/foo.json), causing the wholefile coder to write content to the wrong path. The intended file becomes a 0-byte stub. This is a recurring data-integrity issue observed across multiple dispatch runs over 4 days — not a one-off, but a systemic failure when using small models with absolute file paths. Directly impacts the core edit loop.

source_issues.title: Edit-block path doubling: small models hallucinate prefix-doubled headers; existing prepended-dir guard misses multi-segment cases
source_issues.evidence: Observed across ≥6 dispatches over 4-day window. Files written to doubled paths (e.g. <root>/.claude/.claude/claude-mem.config.json); canonical path ends up as 0-byte stub or empty. Existing prepended-dir guard only handles single-segment cases. Triggers with --file absolute paths and dense --read context.

signals.topic: Local/small LLM models refuse to make file edits, asking users to copy-paste instead

This prevents a legitimate evaluation workflow (validating tool calls in realtime API), not a cosmetic or edge-case issue. Count=1 limits to P1, but user impact is clear.

signals.topic: OpenAI embeddings provider ignores passthrough props, blocking RAG dimension evaluation
signals.summary: The OpenAI embedding provider does not respect 'passthrough' parameters and does not expose a 'dimensions' parameter, preventing users from comparing RAG pipeline performance at different embedding dimensions.
signals.review_reason: Functional bug that prevents users from controlling embedding dimensions, directly blocking RAG pipeline performance evaluation use case. Code-level discrepancy confirmed: embedding.ts does not honor passthrough while responses.ts does. User has a clear real-world evaluation need that is unmet.

source_issues.evidence: User reports that OpenAI embedding provider ignores 'passthrough' props and has no 'dimensions' parameter, blocking RAG pipeline evaluation at different dimensions. Code reference confirms discrepancy with responses API provider which does honor passthrough.

signals.topic: Image/Index node fetching regression breaks query engine after v0.12.49 refactor
signals.summary: After PR #19382 removed the docstore existence check, Image/Index nodes are always fetched from the docstore. Users without a persistent docstore (e.g., OpenSearch vector store) find their previously working queries fail with `ValueError: Document {node_id} is not a Node.` in v0.12.49+.
aliases: Image node retrieval fails after refactor
docstore dependency regression for Image/Index nodes
signals.review_reason: This is a regression bug introduced in v0.12.49 that breaks a previously working retrieval workflow. Users with OpenSearch (or similar vector stores without persistent docstores) find their Image/Index node queries fail entirely with ValueError, rendering the query engine non-functional for these node types. The issue explicitly confirms the exact regression point (PR #19382) and provides a clear failure mode.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Breaking Image/Index node fetching behavior after refactor
source_issues.evidence: User reports queries worked fine on v0.12.48, fail on v0.12.49+ with ValueError. Regression introduced by PR #19382 which removed docstore existence check. Users without persistent docstores (OpenSearch) can no longer retrieve Image/Index nodes.

signals.topic: Workflow step-wise execution deadlocks when @step functions contain async operations
signals.summary: WorkflowHandler.run_step() and Workflow._start()._task() are not synchronized; asyncio.sleep(0) in run_step() yields control before the wait() call in _task() fires, causing deadlock. The step-wise execution API is fundamentally broken for any step with await.
signals.review_reason: The core Workflow step-wise execution feature is broken due to a race condition on a condition variable. Any step function that uses `await` (including asyncio.sleep, HTTP calls, or any async operation) will cause deadlock. This is not an edge case — it is a fundamental blocker for the step-wise debugging API.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Llama Index Workflow: step-wise does not work
source_issues.evidence: Bug report provides code showing deadlock: run_step() calls notify() before Workflow._start()._task() calls wait() on the same condition variable, triggered by asyncio.sleep(0). The provided test case demonstrates handler.run_step() never completes.

signals.topic: PydanticUserError crashes OllamaEmbedding setup due to deprecated __modify_schema__ in Pydantic v2
signals.summary: OllamaEmbedding (and base embedding) imports Embeddings from langchain bridge which uses the deprecated Pydantic v1 __modify_schema__ method, causing PydanticUserError at initialization time for all Ollama users.
aliases: Pydantic v2 compatibility error on Ollama setup
signals.review_reason: PydanticUserError is a hard crash that occurs at initialization for all users setting up OllamaEmbedding. This blocks the entire Ollama integration from functioning, which is a primary use case. The error is deterministic and reproducible by anyone following the documented setup.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: PydanticUserError: The `__modify_schema__` method is not supported in Pydantic v2. Use `__get_pydantic_json_schema__` instead in class `SecretStr`.
source_issues.evidence: Users following the standard Ollama setup pattern (Settings.llm = Ollama, Settings.embed_model = OllamaEmbedding) encounter PydanticUserError at import time due to __modify_schema__ being called in langchain bridge code. Blocks entire Ollama integration.

signals.topic: ContextVar not propagated when FunctionTool uses sync fn (vs async_fn)
signals.summary: When FunctionTool is defined with fn= (sync) instead of async_fn=, ContextVars set by the calling context are not correctly propagated into the tool execution, causing context-dependent features (logging, tracing, auth) to silently fail or return wrong values.
aliases: ContextVar loss in sync FunctionTool execution
contextvars not thread-safe in tool execution
signals.review_reason: ContextVar propagation failure in sync tool execution breaks any context-dependent behavior (logging, tracing, auth, request-scoped state) for users who define FunctionTools as sync functions rather than async. This is a non-obvious failure that silently produces wrong results, making it difficult to debug.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: `ContextVar` not propagated on non-`async` tool execution.
source_issues.evidence: Bug report includes a unit test that reproduces the issue: ContextVar.get() returns wrong value when FunctionTool is defined with fn= vs async_fn=. The issue is confirmed across LlamaIndex core >= 0.14.18.

signals.topic: gemini-embedding-2 silently ignores task_type causing silent accuracy loss in retrieval embeddings
signals.summary: LlamaIndex passes task_type inside EmbedContentConfig for gemini-embedding-2, but Google deprecated this parameter. The backend silently ignores it and embeds raw text without task-specific optimization, causing massive accuracy degradation that users won't notice.
signals.review_reason: gemini-embedding-2 users receive silently degraded embeddings because the task_type parameter is ignored. Users believe they are using optimized retrieval embeddings, but the model falls back to raw text embedding. This is a critical accuracy issue for RAG pipelines that users cannot detect without external evaluation.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: gemini-embedding-2 task instructions not implemented (task_type deprecated)
source_issues.evidence: Google's API now requires task instruction string prefixes (e.g., 'task: search result | query: {text}') for gemini-embedding-2. LlamaIndex still passes the deprecated task_type parameter, which the API ignores. Users get unoptimized embeddings without knowing it.

signals.topic: Windows: daemon orphan processes accumulate, killStaleDaemons silently no-ops, crash recovery fails to detect in-flight workers
signals.summary: On Windows, killStaleDaemons uses POSIX 'ps' which doesn't exist — error is swallowed. Orphan daemon processes from crashed lifetimes accumulate. Crash recovery also fails to detect in-flight headless workers — daemon-state.json doesn't track 'started but not finished' workers, leaving orphan worker processes holding API credits and memory for 5-15 minutes.
aliases: crash recovery in-flight worker state inconsistency
signals.review_reason: User pain point: (1) Windows users face cumulative daemon orphan accumulation with no cleanup path. (2) All users face silent daemon crashes (no log entry) with in-flight workers leaking for 5-15 min and holding API credits. Count=3 (issues #1855, #1856, #1857) confirms this is a sustained systemic problem. Orphan workers holding API credits = direct cost impact.

source_issues.title: Windows: killStaleDaemons silently no-ops because POSIX `ps` isn't available
source_issues.evidence: killStaleDaemons in commands/daemon.ts shells out to 'ps -eo pid,command'. On Windows that command doesn't exist; try/catch swallows the error. Result: orphan daemon start --foreground processes from previous crashed lifetimes accumulate on Windows. Same issue on busybox/Alpine.

source_issues.title: Daemon: detect in-flight worker as failure on crash recovery (transactional state)
source_issues.evidence: daemon-state.json tracks runCount and successCount but neither tracks 'started, never finished'. Workers mid-flight at crash look idle on restart. Operators see runCount > successCount + failureCount discrepancy. Orphan workers hold API credits and memory for 5-15 minutes.

source_issues.title: Daemon crash-recovery: no uncaughtException handler + orphan worker tracking
source_issues.evidence: No uncaughtException/unhandledRejection handlers registered in worker daemon. Any thrown error from timer callback, worker logic, or transitive import crashes daemon silently. PID file and in-flight worker children leak. processPool holds child references in memory only — no on-disk record of owned PIDs, so next daemon start can't reap orphans.

signals.topic: ruflo-core plugin v0.2.0 PostToolUse hooks broken — Bash hook errors on multi-line commands, Edit hook poisons AgentDB with wrong filenames

The Edit hook fires but stores the literal string 'true' as the filename instead of the actual path, poisoning AgentDB/ReasoningBank with wrong data for every file edit. (2) Edit hook silently corrupts AgentDB storage with wrong filenames, poisoning adaptive learning data. Count=2 (issues #1859 and #1862) confirms this affects multiple users. source_issues.title: ruflo-core plugin v0.2.0: PostToolUse hook fails with --format true (v3 CLI regression)

Must be one of: text, json, table'. v3 CLI parser defines --format as string with specific choices; --format true (boolean) is rejected. Hook fires on every file edit in Claude Code.

signals.topic: MCP V3 HTTP server returns non-spec protocolVersion object causing Zod validation error and full MCP connection failure
signals.summary: V3 HTTP MCP server's initialize response returns protocolVersion as {major,minor,patch} object instead of the spec-required YYYY-MM-DD string. Claude Code's MCP client validates with Zod and rejects with 'expected string, received object' — all MCP connections fail silently with no fallback.
signals.review_reason: User pain point: all MCP connections to ruflo are completely blocked. The Zod validation is a hard rejection with no fallback, meaning the entire MCP integration is unusable for affected users. This is a main-flow failure confirmed by explicit error logs.

source_issues.title: V3 HTTP MCP server returns non-spec `protocolVersion` object — Claude Code rejects with Zod error
source_issues.evidence: Claude Code MCP client validates protocolVersion with Zod and rejects with 'expected string, received object'. Result: all MCP connections fail with 'ruflo: http://<host>:8080/mcp (HTTP) - Failed to connect'. Error appears in mcp-logs. Server returns {major:2025,minor:11,patch:25} instead of spec string.

signals.topic: Five integration test failures expose real production bugs in memory persistence, swarm error handling, workflow pause/resume and nested workflows
signals.summary: Five integration tests in v3/__tests__/integration/ fail with real assertion errors: HybridBackend returns undefined on reopen (memory persistence broken), SwarmCoordinator doesn't catch agent errors, agent scaling accumulates instead of replacing, workflow.pauseWorkflow() doesn't actually pause, nested workflows don't resolve sub-workflow results.
signals.review_reason: User pain point: multiple core features are broken in production code — memory persistence, swarm coordination, workflow state management. Each bug is independently confirmed by failing integration tests and represents real feature unavailability. The CI skip policy explicitly classifies these as 'real production bugs, not environmental issues'.

source_issues.title: 5 integration tests reveal real bugs in swarm/workflow/memory persistence
source_issues.evidence: 5 distinct real production bugs identified: (1) HybridBackend stores then reopens DB and gets undefined — SQLite write not fsynced or path mismatch. (2) SwarmCoordinator.executeTask() doesn't catch errors from agent.executeTask(). (3) scaleAgents() accumulates instead of replacing — down-scaling broken. (4) pauseWorkflow() returns without pausing — workflow completes in background. (5) Nested workflow execution doesn't resolve sub-workflow results. All tests skipped with .skip in CI per 'CI must be 100% or skip' policy.

signals.topic: ruflo update fails on Node 26 due to better-sqlite3 native module not compiled for Node 26 V8
signals.summary: better-sqlite3@^11.0.0 cannot compile against Node 26's V8 engine. The alpha.17 release is set as 'latest' and 'alpha' dist-tag, so default npx ruflo@latest install is broken on Node 26. Users must pin to 3.6.12 as workaround, meaning they cannot use the latest version.
aliases: native module compilation fails on Node 26
signals.review_reason: User pain point: installation is completely blocked on Node 26. Since the alpha is tagged as 'latest', users who run default install commands get a node-gyp wall of text and no functional ruflo. source_issues.title: ruflo update fails on Node 26: better-sqlite3 native build error (3.7.0-alpha.17)

signals.topic: Chrome Helper subprocesses (GPU/Renderer) not cleaned up after abnormal session termination
signals.summary: When the agent-browser process is killed or times out, Chrome Helper processes remain as orphans consuming ~100% CPU each (~300% total), persisting until Chrome's watchdog reaps them.

signals.topic: xAI Grok models reject `additionalProperties: false` — tool calling completely broken

signals.review_reason: Three bugs share a common root cause: SDK schema/API serialization generates incompatible values for provider-specific constraints. Issue #14678 completely breaks tool calling for all xAI/Grok users (workaround = disable tools entirely). Issue #12687 blocks Azure stateless/serverless deployments. Issue #15042 breaks all multi-step Cerebras agent flows. All three have reproduction steps, confirmed user impact, and no acceptable workaround.

source_issues.title: addAdditionalPropertiesToJsonSchema breaks xAI/Grok tool calling: xAI rejects additionalProperties: false
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug: SDK adds `additionalProperties: false` to all object schemas, xAI validator rejects property schema 'false'. signals.topic: AI Gateway intermittent GatewayTimeoutError/GatewayResponseError/AbortError under normal production load
signals.summary: AI Gateway randomly throws GatewayTimeoutError, GatewayResponseError, and AbortError under normal production load (~50-100 concurrent calls). Affects both generateText and ToolLoopAgent workflows. The errors fire within ~900ms despite 90s timeout, suggesting gateway-level connection drops rather than real timeouts. No fix available; users need to wrap every model with a doGenerate/doStream proxy for fallback routing.
signals.review_reason: Major production reliability issue. Errors are intermittent but directly affect core operations (generateText, ToolLoopAgent) under normal production load. No acceptable workaround — users must implement their own model proxy with fallback routing, which should not be necessary at the SDK level.

source_issues.title: AI Gateway intermittently throws GatewayResponseError, GatewayTimeoutError, and AbortError under normal production load
source_issues.evidence: Full stress test reproduction script provided. Errors fire at ~900ms despite 90s timeout config — gateway is dropping connections, not a real timeout. Affects all model providers through the gateway. Only workaround: wrap every model with a doGenerate/doStream proxy that retries via different gateway. No acceptable fix exists for users.

signals.topic: MockLanguageModelV3/V4 off-by-one bug — first array entry skipped in doGenerate/doStream/doEmbed
signals.summary: When MockLanguageModelV3 or MockLanguageModelV4 is constructed with an array of results, the first call returns the second array entry instead of the first (index off-by-one). The same bug exists in MockEmbeddingModelV3/V4.doEmbed. This silently malfunctions multi-round conversation test scenarios (e.g. tool-call → tool-result → final text), with no error thrown — the agent just sees wrong responses or may terminate prematurely.
signals.review_reason: Affects test infrastructure used by any developer writing multi-round agent tests. Silent failure with no error thrown means tests pass incorrectly, which can lead to shipping broken agent logic. Root cause and fix identified.

source_issues.title: Bug: MockLanguageModelV3 / V4 array form for doGenerate/doStream skips first entry (off-by-one)
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified in code: `doGenerateCalls.push(options)` increments length, then `doGenerate[this.doGenerateCalls.length]` indexes from 1 instead of 0. Silent failure — no error thrown, output just diverges. Most natural use case (deterministic multi-round testing) malfunctions. PR offer pending.

signals.topic: @opentelemetry/api hard-pin (exact version) causes duplicate package installs, breaking child span context propagation
signals.summary: ai@6.0.176 hard-pins @opentelemetry/api to exact version 1.9.0. When an application uses @opentelemetry/api@1.9.1, npm installs two physical copies of the OpenTelemetry API. signals.review_reason: Silently corrupts observability data. Child spans disappearing while root spans still export creates a deceptive debugging picture — users may not notice until important traces are missing. Requires manual package-manager override as fix.

source_issues.title: Bug: `ai` hard-pins `@opentelemetry/api@1.9.0`, causing lost traces when app uses `^1.9.1`
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate @opentelemetry/api packages installed. Child spans disappear while root spans still export. Requires package-manager override to fix. Affects observability — critical for production debugging.

signals.topic: Underscore-prefixed route layouts cause TypeScript type errors in Next.js 16 dev mode

signals.topic: CLI `vercel env add --value` silently stores empty string — regression blocks production deployments

User impact is production-critical: HMAC keys, signing keys, and API credentials silently become empty strings, causing runtime failures in deployed applications with no error message from CLI. CI/CD automation scripts are directly blocked.

signals.topic: @vercel/react-router Skew Protection cookie not injected for nodejs runtime — feature effectively disabled
signals.summary: The @vercel/react-router Vite plugin only injects the Vercel entry server (which sets the `__vdpl` Skew Protection cookie) for edge runtime routes. Routes using the default nodejs runtime fall back to React Router's built-in entry.server, disabling Skew Protection despite it being enabled in the dashboard. After each deploy, users with cached HTML get 404s for old content-hashed asset chunks.
aliases: Skew Protection cookie missing nodejs runtime
signals.review_reason: P1: Skew Protection — a critical deployment safety feature — is silently non-functional for the default nodejs runtime in @vercel/react-router. Users enable Skew Protection in the dashboard expecting deployment safety, but it has zero effect on nodejs routes. User-visible symptom: after every deploy, users with cached HTML get 404s for stale asset chunks. This is a misleading feature gap — the feature appears enabled but is actually disabled.

source_issues.title: @vercel/react-router: Skew Protection entry.server only injected for edge runtime, not nodejs
source_issues.evidence: Verified via curl: `curl -sI <deployment-url>` on a nodejs runtime deployment shows no `Set-Cookie: __vdpl=...` header, while edge runtime deployments have it. After deploys, clients with cached HTML get 404s for old content-hashed asset chunks because Skew Protection is silently non-functional.

This breaks expected CLI patterns and blocks AI tooling integration.
signals.review_reason: P2: The `vercel logs` CLI command lacks historical log retrieval capability and hangs indefinitely without live traffic, forcing developers to the web dashboard. While this is a significant CLI UX gap, it is classified as P2 because it is a feature deficiency rather than a main-flow blocking bug — logs can still be accessed via the web dashboard. However, it blocks AI tooling integration and non-interactive debugging workflows.

source_issues.title: Historical logs in `vercel logs` command
source_issues.evidence: Documented current behavior: `vercel logs` hangs indefinitely at 'waiting for new logs...' when no traffic is occurring. No flags exist to retrieve historical logs. Developers must use the web dashboard (vercel.com → project → Functions → Logs) for any historical log inspection. AI tooling (Cursor, Claude Code) cannot access historical logs via CLI.

signals.topic: Debug gutter: right-click "Set Breakpoint" places breakpoint on wrong line
signals.summary: When gutter is customized to show only line numbers, right-clicking the line number to set a breakpoint places it on a different line than clicked. This causes developers to set breakpoints on unintended lines, potentially wasting debugging time or missing bugs.
aliases: breakpoint placed on wrong line gutter
signals.review_reason: This is a real user pain point because it directly breaks the core debugging workflow: setting a breakpoint on the wrong line wastes developer time, causes confusion, and could result in missed bugs. Even at count=1, the impact is high — debugging is a primary IDE function and wrong breakpoint placement leads to debugging the wrong code entirely.

source_issues.title: Incorrect SetBreakpoint behavior on gutter
source_issues.evidence: Right-clicking a line number with only line numbers visible in gutter sets breakpoint on wrong line. User explicitly reports the breakpoint appears on the wrong line, which directly breaks the core debugging workflow — developers cannot reliably set breakpoints on intended lines.

signals.topic: VS Code settings import dialog: keyboard Enter does not confirm "Ok" action
signals.summary: On Linux Wayland (and likely other platforms), pressing Enter in the VS Code import confirmation dialog does not trigger the import action — the dialog closes but no settings are imported and no confirmation toast appears. Users are forced to click "Ok" with the mouse, breaking expected keyboard-driven workflow.
aliases: Import dialog Enter key not working
VS Code import confirmation dialog broken keyboard support
signals.review_reason: This is a real user pain point: the VS Code import dialog is a primary migration path for Zed users coming from VS Code, and the Enter key — the universal keyboard shortcut for confirming dialogs — is completely non-functional. Users are forced to use the mouse, breaking keyboard-driven workflow and blocking the expected onboarding/migration experience.

source_issues.title: Enter does not confirm Import dialog box
source_issues.evidence: User reports that pressing Enter after focusing "Ok" in the import confirmation dialog closes the dialog without importing settings or showing a confirmation toast. Only clicking "Ok" with the mouse triggers the action. Reporter notes the same issue may affect other dialog boxes. 2 comments from other users confirming similar experience.

signals.topic: Auto-indent inserts extra empty lines when pressing Enter with "Show Whitespaces" enabled
signals.summary: On Windows 10, when "Show Whitespaces" is set to All, pressing Enter on a line with existing indentation inserts a spurious empty line in addition to the expected behavior. This actively disrupts typing flow and makes the editor unusable for users who prefer visible whitespace.
aliases: Enter creates extra empty lines with whitespace display
signals.review_reason: This is a real user pain point: auto-indentation is a fundamental text editing feature used on every keystroke. The bug actively disrupts the primary typing workflow, and users who prefer visible whitespace (a legitimate and common preference) are forced to disable a useful setting to work around a Zed regression. This qualifies as a main flow failure with clear user impact.

source_issues.title: Auto Indent insert empty lines
source_issues.evidence: User reports that with show_whitespaces=all enabled, pressing Enter on a line with 3 tabs produces an extra empty line on each keystroke. Provides screenshot showing the incorrect (extra empty line) vs expected behavior. Windows 10 user, reproducible 100% of the time.

signals.topic: Agent panel loses keyboard focus after confirming MCP tool permission prompts
signals.summary: When using the Agent panel with MCP tool calls that require permission confirmation, pressing Enter or clicking "Allow Once" to approve a tool causes focus to jump from the Agent panel back to the editor pane. This happens repeatedly during active MCP-heavy sessions (roughly every minute), forcing users to manually re-focus the agent input to continue their conversation.
aliases: focus stolen from agent panel after tool permission
MCP tool permission dialog focus bug
signals.review_reason: This is a real user pain point: Agent panel focus is repeatedly stolen after every tool permission confirmation (roughly every minute during active use). Users must manually re-focus to continue interacting with the agent, creating a persistent, interruptive workflow disruption during a core Zed feature (Agent/AI integration). The codebase itself acknowledges focus-steal as a known concern, further validating this as a genuine bug.

source_issues.title: Agent panel loses focus to editor after confirming tool permission prompts
source_issues.evidence: User reports focus jumps from agent panel to editor pane after every tool permission confirmation during MCP-heavy sessions. Occurs on macOS with latest stable Zed. 1 comment confirms. User needs to manually re-focus with Cmd-? to continue agent interaction. Issue references existing test 'test_vim_search_does_not_steal_focus_from_agent_panel', confirming focus-steal is a known concern.
